problem: PixelGoal navigation needs metric target grounding and obstacle-aware local planning, but PixelGoal policies lack metric grounding from temporal context, while geometry-aware local planners assume metric PointGoal inputs. Image-space goal grounding and local 3D reasoning remain disconnected in trajectory generation.
motivation: PixelGoal is a natural interface between VLM high-level reasoning and low-level navigation, without needing a map or metric goal. Depth-based back-projection of the pixel fails under occlusion or sensor noise, and a point goal alone does not encode traversability. Scalable 3D occupancy supervision for navigation is also lacking.
key_idea: Ground the PixelGoal into an egocentric metric goal representation via auxiliary prediction and feed goal-conditioned local occupancy tokens together with it to a diffusion trajectory planner, with occupancy labels generated from monocular RGB videos (L3ROcc).
insight: The ablation shows that each component contributes: goal grounding lowers ADE from 0.164 to 0.150 m, occupancy supervision alone lowers it to 0.146, and directly exposing goal-conditioned occupancy tokens to the planner gives the best ADE/FDE (0.130/0.135 m) despite a slightly lower occupancy IoU. Occupancy IoU is therefore not a good measure of planning utility, and direct conditioning matters more than auxiliary supervision. A PixelGoal without grounding is insufficient: NavDP with a PixelGoal loses over 50 SR points.
method: L3ROcc: runs π^3 on sampled monocular RGB frames to get pointmaps and poses, filters low-confidence points and depth edges, interpolates poses (cubic spline + SLERP), fixes metric scale from a reference trajectory or sensor depth, then does Occ3D-style ray casting to produce visible-occupancy and visibility-mask labels (100x140x60 grid at 4 cm) plus aligned trajectory labels.
Shared RGB-D encoder: DINOv2-S/14 RGB encoder plus a conv depth encoder, fused into spatial geometry tokens, refined geometry tokens and per-frame scene tokens over an 8-frame history.

Goal and scene conditioning: Fourier-feature MLP encodes the (u,v) pixel goal; a goal-conditioned learnable query cross-attends the context (scene tokens + current spatial token) to produce an ego-goal token z_e, supervised by an auxiliary egocentric goal head (x,y,heading); a state pooler gives z_s.

Planning-oriented occupancy encoding: learned 2D-to-3D lifting of the refined tokens into an occupancy feature volume, decoded by a 3D conv head with focal loss (occupied positive; free and unobserved negative). The volume is pooled into memory tokens and read by K=8 goal-conditioned queries into Z_occ, which stays differentiable for the trajectory loss.
Diffusion planner: a DDPM diffusion transformer denoises 24 motion increments (dx,dy,dtheta) conditioned on [timestep, z_e, z_s, U_ctx, Z_occ], using 10 denoising steps.
Joint loss: weighted sum of noise-prediction Smooth-L1, trajectory reprojection to image (uv), ego-goal regression and occupancy focal loss, with weights (0.8, 1.0, 0.25, 1.0).
Deployment stack: SAM 3 updates the pixel goal at 1 Hz, Dynamic-VINS gives odometry, MPC tracks the waypoints, and the last target position is propagated when the target is out of view.

setting.backbone: OccPlanner: DINOv2-S/14 RGB encoder + conv depth encoder + diffusion transformer (trained end-to-end)
setting.training_data: Over 200,000 expert trajectories from InternData-N1 (simulated indoor, differential-drive, RGB-D), with L3ROcc occupancy annotations; real-world fine-tuning on 829 L3ROcc-annotated samples
setting.observation: 8-frame RGB-D history (224x224) plus a normalized pixel goal
setting.action_space: 24 predicted local trajectory increments (dx,dy,dtheta) tracked by an MPC controller
setting.privileged: none (the pixel goal is reprojected from the fixed target by the simulator at each step; the target is initially visible)

numbers.eval_set_note: Medium split 3-5 m, 2,437 filtered episodes across 60 unseen scenes (20 Home)
numbers.extra: trained on InternData-N1 with L3ROcc occupancy; success radius 0.5 m
fine-tuned on 829 real-world L3ROcc-annotated samples; success within 0.5 m; CR = collision rate (5/20)
numbers.evidence: Table 3: Real-world fine-tuned 16/20 SR, 5/20 CR; text: SR from 55% to 80%, collision rate from 60% to 25%

numbers_note: No standard benchmarks; results are on the authors' own InternScenes closed-loop protocol (split labelled 'test' as a placeholder for unseen scenes). Open-loop ablation (Table 2, 1,496 held-out InternData-N1 samples): OccPlanner ADE 0.130, FDE 0.135, AHE 9.99, FHE 15.31, IoU 47.02.
results: OccPlanner beats the PixelGoal baselines (NavDP-PixelGoal, PixNav) in all eight scene-distance settings, e.g. 94.78 vs 18.45 SR in hard-split Cluttered Easy. It also beats PointGoal NavDP, ViPlanner and LoGoPlanner, and stays within 2.24 and 3.50 mean SR points of the strongest reference, iPlanner, which receives the metric goal. Real-world fine-tuning raises Go2 SR from 55% to 80% and reduces collisions from 60% to 25%.
limitations: No explicit whole-body clearance constraint and no persistent occupancy memory, so contacts happen after obstacles leave the camera view.
L3ROcc assumes static scenes, so moving objects contaminate the reconstructed geometry.
The occupancy branch relies heavily on depth input, and evaluation is on the authors' own protocol with only 20 real-world trials per setting.
